title: Commodification of Intelligence: Good, Bad, and Ugly Circular AI Deals
excerpt: Circular AI deals aren't just bubble behavior: they mirror how commodity industries finance capital-intensive infrastructure. When circular deals are healthy — and when they hide risk.
content_html:
Every few months, and especially this week, the AI space gets criticized for circular financing and customer relationships. OpenAI raises money from Microsoft, spending it on Microsoft servers; Nvidia backstops CoreWeave debt, and CoreWeave buys Nvidia GPUs. “The bubble is about to burst!” analysts scream.

Analysts point to dot-com deals with circular investments in 1999, arguing that this is all bound to happen again[1][2]. They are wrong.

Circular deals are more interesting than “good” or “bad.” They show the AI industry isn't just maturing, but modifying the idea of “AI” to something that is less a technology product, and more a commodity. Imagine that—intelligence available like electricity, and the underlying financial system structured accordingly.

The evolution of circular deals points to the commodification of AI, where compute capacity is moving from a business model where you buy a product (e.g., the hardware, or space in a data center) to something so fungible that you buy it the way you buy electricity, copper, natural gas, or other commodities.

We'll explore why circular deals are particularly important in commodity industries and what this implies for understanding the trajectory of AI. First we'll cover how major investments in traditional commodities markets work to ground our analogy more clearly. Next, we'll cover the investments that mimic this process in AI, showing how such investments can be healthy. Finally, we'll explore a few examples where circular deals do not abide by this analogy and how these deals are introducing risks that could one day turn into awful surprises for the companies themselves, their investors, or the entire sector.

Buying and Selling Commodities: A Circularity Primer

Complex commodity infrastructure like mines, refineries, and ports comes with such large development costs that a bank lending a development company money can potentially risk its own solvency in doing so. Circular deals with multiple customers or beneficiaries, and potentially even governments, are often the only solution that gets shovels in dirt or ships in the water.

Let's look at a simplified example of such a deal. Imagine you want to develop your region's economy with several wells and a pipeline, and you can't afford it. You partner with a commodity trading firm who agrees to make your company attractive to banks or bond buyers by guaranteeing they will buy all your oil at a certain price. This means you are guaranteed revenue for the foreseeable future, and the banks know they can trust you'll repay their loans. The trading firm might even take an equity stake in your company for good measure—potentially to encourage better governance or oversight.

With such a relationship between you and the oil trader, you've got oil, a large bank loan, and a guaranteed customer… you've got yourself a circular commodities deal!

This is not a contrived example; it's a common strategy developed and evolved since the 1960s. Japanese commodities traders and development banks financed infrastructure to enable commodity development, committing to future purchases and equity deals[3]. Jamaica did so in the 1980s[4].

More recently, the US government began facilitating circular deal making to stimulate the critical minerals sector in its bid for supply chain resilience. Last year, MP Materials, a relative newcomer to magnet manufacturing and critical minerals, announced a 10-year relationship with the Department of War, where the latter committed to buying all neodymium-praseodymium (i.e., magnets) from the company for at least $110/kg[5]. Since then, such off-take agreements have been announced between MP Materials and General Motors[6], and are in fact quite common in the electric vehicle space[7]. These direct relationships also incentivize equity ownership in the commodities producers and even underlying mines because it's very clear that these producers and mines will have revenue in the coming years.

Fungible commodities with large global markets are particularly well suited to such deals because the counterparty guaranteeing to be a customer (i.e., the oil trading firm in our example above) knows there is a large market they can tap into. They likely have a history of successfully making such sales, otherwise they wouldn't have billions of dollars and a pristine reputation they can leverage.

AI is Fungible and Expensive to Develop

The frontier generative AI industry—be it model development or inference—is very much dependent on Nvidia. GPUs are effectively a fungible commodity thanks to Nvidia's development of the underlying infrastructure and standardization across all firms in the space. Three forces are enabling AI chips and associated data centers to act like a fungible commodity:

  1. The majority of compute today comes from Nvidia GPUs, so two data centers using similar chips are almost the same for the purposes of hyperscalers, model builders, and those needing inference.
  2. Model development and inference at scale requires massive data centers sometimes costing well over $10 billion. These data centers can't be developed unless it's via a creative financing deal or via a company with access to immense wealth (i.e., the hyperscalers).
  3. Aside from GPUs, memory and other hardware, electricity is the other bottleneck. You can't build an 11-figure data center without access to large amounts of reliable electricity.

As a result, GPUs, electricity, and data centers are all effectively fungible, with large order backlogs and pent-up demand. If you build a data center and can't leverage it for your own business, there's a good chance you can sell it to someone who can—they might even pay a premium for availability in the short term.

SpaceX and Meta, despite trying to build top-tier foundation models, are profitably leasing their own data centers to others—these data centers are working today and ready for frontier lab workloads. Well-capitalized labs are willing to pay a huge premium for the privilege. SpaceX leases its Colossus 1 and 2 data centers for over $2 billion per month[8], at a significant markup over other smaller clouds and data centers[9].

Let's now return to the aspiring startup or neocloud. You are starting up and, like our oil example earlier, have proven yourself on a small scale but now need your own data center or access to thousands of GPUs. What can you do?

Enter Nvidia and the circular deal—much like the oil deal.

Nvidia provides the capital and product access to your startup, prioritizing your access to its GPUs so you can get the hardware you need. Nvidia has a $1 trillion order backlog[10] and knows it can resell your hardware or make better use of it if you fail, so it goes a step further: it becomes the guaranteed buyer of your compute if you can't take advantage of it… much like SpaceX and Meta above. This is not theoretical—SemiAnalysis provides estimates for Nvidia compute off-take agreements and pricing[11]. As with our oil example, Nvidia might want some equity as well—and you will want them to have it, should you need to call in any favors later.

This is, of course, one type of circular deal, and a relatively simple one at that. It's been used in CoreWeave's $6.3 billion deal with Nvidia[12], alongside smaller data center operators like Firmus ($505 million[13]).

This helps explain why we see so many interconnecting and circular relationships—OpenAI cancels its deal with Oracle, so Meta swoops in[14]; SpaceX leases servers to Google, Google invests in Anthropic; and so on.

Wall Street gets circular deals, and humanity gets artificial general intelligence… purportedly.

When Circular Deals Go Ugly

Nvidia argues it is supporting a global AI ecosystem. Unfortunately, this doesn't preclude it from overextending itself. A $6.3 billion deal with CoreWeave is one thing, but committing up to $750 billion[2] is another.

The success of this approach for startups and neoclouds also assumes that AI and data centers continue to be fungible and “resellable”. Should standards or chipsets change, or should technologies make it easier to run local models or models on small clusters, then the business models might fail and the off-take agreements Nvidia has might not help the ecosystem much.

… and When They Go Bad

Circularity becomes particularly nefarious when it is used to hide the effects of the investments, debts, or other obligations from investors.

Figure 1 shows the FT's[15] breakdown of a recent TeraWulf bond deal. In this case, TeraWulf can obtain financing given Google's backstop of any lease failures, should Fluidstack not be able to pay TeraWulf, or Anthropic unable to pay Fluidstack[16]. Google is skipping the entire reselling process and simply committing to cover any delinquencies. This gives TeraWulf the benefits of Google acting as a guarantor of the loan without the loan appearing on Google's balance sheet.

Similarly, Meta's $27.3 billion Hyperion data center bond sale is an off-balance sheet one[17], as is its more recent $12.3 billion deal marketed by BlackRock[18].

Many finance professionals argue that these bonds are ultimately guaranteed by the impressive and continually growing revenues and profits from the hyperscalers, so there is nothing to worry about. The reason these bonds find so many customers, despite the circularity label, is that the final guarantors (i.e., the hyperscalers) generate billions of dollars of profit every year and can easily cover these costs, should it come down to that.

… but this is today, and it's with the current bond deals. Will tomorrow's bond deals be supported by the hyperscalers in the same way? And what happens if hyperscaler revenue trends change? What if the banks begin expanding the backstop agreements from hyperscalers to “generally pretty decent” companies? What if the backstop fails to be enforced? Will we see hyperscaler-backstop-backed-bonds grouped together, collateralized, and resold the way Mortgage Backed Securities were in 2007?[19]

Implications and Conclusion

Circular deals are not bad. In fact, they are critical in the development of the AI ecosystem much like such deals are used in critical minerals, oil, electric vehicles, and other capital intensive industries with incredibly high startup costs.

The circularity helps illustrate the commodification of AI today, and how the technology might one day be more like electricity or an internet connection, rather than a product one buys or subscribes to.

When circular deals are supported by overextended lenders, or when overextended lenders try to move such deals off their balance sheets, they become ugly and bad—in other words, incredibly risky. This industry is likely to grow much more in the coming years, so it is important to watch for the lowering of standards or aggregation of risk. As SemiAnalysis writes[11]:

AI Debt Financing will become a multi-trillion-dollar credit market, with over $7T of debt outstanding by 2029 driven both by AI IT Capex and AI Datacenter Capex needs [...] This will make it the second largest asset backed debt market after the US mortgage-backed financing market at just over $13T.

In this evolution, there might be a few bad deals along the way. It's important to keep your eyes open.

blocks.html_en: More recently, the US government began facilitating circular deal making to stimulate the critical minerals sector in its bid for supply chain resilience. Last year, MP Materials, a relative newcomer to magnet manufacturing and critical minerals, announced a 10-year relationship with the Department of War, where the latter committed to buying all neodymium-praseodymium (i.e., magnets) from the company for at least $110/kg[5]. Since then, such off-take agreements have been announced between MP Materials and General Motors[6], and are in fact quite common in the electric vehicle space[7]. These direct relationships also incentivize equity ownership in the commodities producers and even underlying mines because it's very clear that these producers and mines will have revenue in the coming years.

sentences.en: More recently, the US government began facilitating circular deal making to stimulate the critical minerals sector in its bid for supply chain resilience.
sentences.zh: 最近，美国政府开始促进循环交易，以刺激关键矿产行业，以增强供应链的弹性。

sentences.en: Last year, MP Materials, a relative newcomer to magnet manufacturing and critical minerals, announced a 10-year relationship with the Department of War, where the latter committed to buying all neodymium-praseodymium (i.e., magnets) from the company for at least $110/kg[5].
sentences.zh: 去年，磁铁制造和关键矿物领域相对较新的 MP Materials 宣布与美国陆军部建立为期 10 年的合作关系，后者承诺以至少 110 美元/公斤的价格从该公司购买所有钕镨（即磁铁）[5]。

sentences.en: Since then, such off-take agreements have been announced between MP Materials and General Motors[6], and are in fact quite common in the electric vehicle space[7].
sentences.zh: 此后，MP Materials 和通用汽车之间宣布了此类承购协议[6]，并且实际上在电动汽车领域非常常见[7]。

sentences.en: These direct relationships also incentivize equity ownership in the commodities producers and even underlying mines because it's very clear that these producers and mines will have revenue in the coming years.
sentences.zh: 这些直接关系还激励了大宗商品生产商甚至底层矿山的股权，因为很明显这些生产商和矿山将在未来几年获得收入。

blocks.html_en: Fungible commodities with large global markets are particularly well suited to such deals because the counterparty guaranteeing to be a customer (i.e., the oil trading firm in our example above) knows there is a large market they can tap into. They likely have a history of successfully making such sales, otherwise they wouldn't have billions of dollars and a pristine reputation they can leverage.

sentences.en: Fungible commodities with large global markets are particularly well suited to such deals because the counterparty guaranteeing to be a customer (i.e., the oil trading firm in our example above) knows there is a large market they can tap into.
sentences.zh: 具有大型全球市场的可替代商品特别适合此类交易，因为保证成为客户的交易对手（即上面示例中的石油贸易公司）知道他们可以进入一个巨大的市场。

sentences.en: They likely have a history of successfully making such sales, otherwise they wouldn't have billions of dollars and a pristine reputation they can leverage.
sentences.zh: 他们可能有成功进行此类销售的历史，否则他们就不会拥有数十亿美元和可以利用的原始声誉。

blocks.html_en: AI is Fungible and Expensive to Develop

sentences.en: AI is Fungible and Expensive to Develop
sentences.zh: 人工智能是可替代的且开发成本昂贵

blocks.html_en: The frontier generative AI industry—be it model development or inference—is very much dependent on Nvidia. GPUs are effectively a fungible commodity thanks to Nvidia's development of the underlying infrastructure and standardization across all firms in the space. Three forces are enabling AI chips and associated data centers to act like a fungible commodity:

sentences.en: The frontier generative AI industry—be it model development or inference—is very much dependent on Nvidia.
sentences.zh: 前沿的生成式 AI 行业——无论是模型开发还是推理——都非常依赖 Nvidia。

sentences.en: GPUs are effectively a fungible commodity thanks to Nvidia's development of the underlying infrastructure and standardization across all firms in the space.
sentences.zh: 由于 Nvidia 开发了底层基础设施以及该领域所有公司的标准化，GPU 实际上是一种可替代的商品。

sentences.en: Three forces are enabling AI chips and associated data centers to act like a fungible commodity:
sentences.zh: 三种力量使人工智能芯片和相关数据中心能够像可替代商品一样发挥作用：

blocks.html_en: • The majority of compute today comes from Nvidia GPUs, so two data centers using similar chips are almost the same for the purposes of hyperscalers, model builders, and those needing inference.

sentences.en: The majority of compute today comes from Nvidia GPUs, so two data centers using similar chips are almost the same for the purposes of hyperscalers, model builders, and those needing inference.
sentences.zh: 如今，大部分计算都来自 Nvidia GPU，因此对于超大规模用户、模型构建者和需要推理的用户来说，使用相似芯片的两个数据中心几乎是相同的。

blocks.html_en: • Model development and inference at scale requires massive data centers sometimes costing well over $10 billion. These data centers can't be developed unless it's via a creative financing deal or via a company with access to immense wealth (i.e., the hyperscalers).

sentences.en: Model development and inference at scale requires massive data centers sometimes costing well over $10 billion.
sentences.zh: 大规模模型开发和推理需要大型数据中心，有时成本远超 100 亿美元。

sentences.en: These data centers can't be developed unless it's via a creative financing deal or via a company with access to immense wealth (i.e., the hyperscalers).
sentences.zh: 除非通过创造性的融资交易或通过拥有巨额财富的公司（即超大规模企业），否则无法开发这些数据中心。

blocks.html_en: • Aside from GPUs, memory and other hardware, electricity is the other bottleneck. You can't build an 11-figure data center without access to large amounts of reliable electricity.

sentences.en: Aside from GPUs, memory and other hardware, electricity is the other bottleneck.
sentences.zh: 除了GPU、内存和其他硬件之外，电力是另一个瓶颈。

sentences.en: You can't build an 11-figure data center without access to large amounts of reliable electricity.
sentences.zh: 如果没有大量可靠的电力，就无法建造 11 位数的数据中心。

blocks.html_en: As a result, GPUs, electricity, and data centers are all effectively fungible, with large order backlogs and pent-up demand. If you build a data center and can't leverage it for your own business, there's a good chance you can sell it to someone who can—they might even pay a premium for availability in the short term.

sentences.en: As a result, GPUs, electricity, and data centers are all effectively fungible, with large order backlogs and pent-up demand.
sentences.zh: 因此，GPU、电力和数据中心都可以有效地替代，并且存在大量订单积压和被压抑的需求。

sentences.en: If you build a data center and can't leverage it for your own business, there's a good chance you can sell it to someone who can—they might even pay a premium for availability in the short term.
sentences.zh: 如果您构建了一个数据中心，但无法将其用于自己的业务，那么您很有可能将其出售给有能力的人，他们甚至可能会在短期内为可用性支付溢价。

blocks.html_en: SpaceX and Meta, despite trying to build top-tier foundation models, are profitably leasing their own data centers to others—these data centers are working today and ready for frontier lab workloads. Well-capitalized labs are willing to pay a huge premium for the privilege. SpaceX leases its Colossus 1 and 2 data centers for over $2 billion per month[8], at a significant markup over other smaller clouds and data centers[9].

sentences.en: SpaceX and Meta, despite trying to build top-tier foundation models, are profitably leasing their own data centers to others—these data centers are working today and ready for frontier lab workloads.
sentences.zh: SpaceX 和 Meta 尽管试图构建顶级基础模型，但仍将自己的数据中心出租给其他公司以盈利——这些数据中心目前正在运行，并为前沿实验室工作负载做好了准备。

sentences.en: Well-capitalized labs are willing to pay a huge premium for the privilege.
sentences.zh: 资本充足的实验室愿意为这一特权支付巨额溢价。

sentences.en: SpaceX leases its Colossus 1 and 2 data centers for over $2 billion per month[8], at a significant markup over other smaller clouds and data centers[9].
sentences.zh: SpaceX 以每月超过 20 亿美元的价格租赁其 Colossus 1 和 2 数据中心[8]，其价格远高于其他小型云和数据中心[9]。

blocks.html_en: Let's now return to the aspiring startup or neocloud. You are starting up and, like our oil example earlier, have proven yourself on a small scale but now need your own data center or access to thousands of GPUs. What can you do?

sentences.en: Let's now return to the aspiring startup or neocloud.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们回到有抱负的初创公司 Neocloud。

sentences.en: You are starting up and, like our oil example earlier, have proven yourself on a small scale but now need your own data center or access to thousands of GPUs.
sentences.zh: 您正在起步，就像我们之前的石油示例一样，已经在小规模上证明了自己，但现在需要自己的数据中心或访问数千个 GPU。

sentences.en: What can you do?
sentences.zh: 你能做什么？

blocks.html_en: Enter Nvidia and the circular deal—much like the oil deal.

sentences.en: Enter Nvidia and the circular deal—much like the oil deal.
sentences.zh: 英伟达和循环交易很像石油交易。

blocks.html_en: Nvidia provides the capital and product access to your startup, prioritizing your access to its GPUs so you can get the hardware you need. Nvidia has a $1 trillion order backlog[10] and knows it can resell your hardware or make better use of it if you fail, so it goes a step further: it becomes the guaranteed buyer of your compute if you can't take advantage of it… much like SpaceX and Meta above. This is not theoretical—SemiAnalysis provides estimates for Nvidia compute off-take agreements and pricing[11]. As with our oil example, Nvidia might want some equity as well—and you will want them to have it, should you need to call in any favors later.

sentences.en: Nvidia provides the capital and product access to your startup, prioritizing your access to its GPUs so you can get the hardware you need.
sentences.zh: Nvidia 为您的初创公司提供资金和产品访问权限，优先让您访问其 GPU，以便您可以获得所需的硬件。

sentences.en: Nvidia has a $1 trillion order backlog[10] and knows it can resell your hardware or make better use of it if you fail, so it goes a step further: it becomes the guaranteed buyer of your compute if you can't take advantage of it…
sentences.zh: Nvidia 拥有 1 万亿美元的积压订单[10]，并且知道如果您失败了，它可以转售您的硬件或更好地利用它，因此它更进一步：如果您无法利用它，它就会成为您的计算的保证买家......

sentences.en: much like SpaceX and Meta above.
sentences.zh: 就像上面的 SpaceX 和 Meta 一样。

sentences.en: This is not theoretical—SemiAnalysis provides estimates for Nvidia compute off-take agreements and pricing[11].
sentences.zh: 这不是理论上的——SemiAnalysis 提供了 Nvidia 计算承购协议和定价的估算[11]。

sentences.en: As with our oil example, Nvidia might want some equity as well—and you will want them to have it, should you need to call in any favors later.
sentences.zh: 与我们的石油例子一样，英伟达可能也想要一些股权——如果你以后需要寻求任何帮助，你会希望他们拥有这些股权。

blocks.html_en: This is, of course, one type of circular deal, and a relatively simple one at that. It's been used in CoreWeave's $6.3 billion deal with Nvidia[12], alongside smaller data center operators like Firmus ($505 million[13]).

sentences.en: This is, of course, one type of circular deal, and a relatively simple one at that.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一种循环交易，而且是一种相对简单的交易。

sentences.en: It's been used in CoreWeave's $6.3 billion deal with Nvidia[12], alongside smaller data center operators like Firmus ($505 million[13]).
sentences.zh: 它已被用于 CoreWeave 与 Nvidia 的 63 亿美元交易[12]，以及 Firmus 等小型数据中心运营商（5.05 亿美元[13]）。

blocks.html_en: This helps explain why we see so many interconnecting and circular relationships—OpenAI cancels its deal with Oracle, so Meta swoops in[14]; SpaceX leases servers to Google, Google invests in Anthropic; and so on.

sentences.en: This helps explain why we see so many interconnecting and circular relationships—OpenAI cancels its deal with Oracle, so Meta swoops in[14]; SpaceX leases servers to Google, Google invests in Anthropic; and so on.
sentences.zh: 这有助于解释为什么我们看到如此多的互连和循环关系——OpenAI 取消了与 Oracle 的交易，因此 Meta 突然介入[14]； SpaceX向谷歌租赁服务器，谷歌投资Anthropic；等等。

blocks.html_en: Wall Street gets circular deals, and humanity gets artificial general intelligence… purportedly.

sentences.en: Wall Street gets circular deals, and humanity gets artificial general intelligence…
sentences.zh: 华尔街获得循环交易，人类获得通用人工智能……

sentences.en: purportedly.
sentences.zh: 据称。

blocks.html_en: When Circular Deals Go Ugly

sentences.en: When Circular Deals Go Ugly
sentences.zh: 当循环交易变得丑陋时

blocks.html_en: Nvidia argues it is supporting a global AI ecosystem. Unfortunately, this doesn't preclude it from overextending itself. A $6.3 billion deal with CoreWeave is one thing, but committing up to $750 billion[2] is another.

sentences.en: Nvidia argues it is supporting a global AI ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 英伟达声称它正在支持全球人工智能生态系统。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, this doesn't preclude it from overextending itself.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这并不妨碍它过度扩张。

sentences.en: A $6.3 billion deal with CoreWeave is one thing, but committing up to $750 billion[2] is another.
sentences.zh: 与 CoreWeave 达成 63 亿美元的交易是一回事，但承诺高达 7500 亿美元[2] 则是另一回事。

blocks.html_en: The success of this approach for startups and neoclouds also assumes that AI and data centers continue to be fungible and “resellable”. Should standards or chipsets change, or should technologies make it easier to run local models or models on small clusters, then the business models might fail and the off-take agreements Nvidia has might not help the ecosystem much.

sentences.en: The success of this approach for startups and neoclouds also assumes that AI and data centers continue to be fungible and “resellable”.
sentences.zh: 这种方法对于初创公司和新云的成功还假设人工智能和数据中心继续可替代和“可转售”。

sentences.en: Should standards or chipsets change, or should technologies make it easier to run local models or models on small clusters, then the business models might fail and the off-take agreements Nvidia has might not help the ecosystem much.
sentences.zh: 如果标准或芯片组发生变化，或者技术应该使本地模型或小型集群上的模型更容易运行，那么商业模式可能会失败，而英伟达的承购协议可能不会对生态系统有太大帮助。

blocks.html_en: … and When They Go Bad

sentences.en: and When They Go Bad
sentences.zh: 当他们变坏时

blocks.html_en: Circularity becomes particularly nefarious when it is used to hide the effects of the investments, debts, or other obligations from investors.

sentences.en: Circularity becomes particularly nefarious when it is used to hide the effects of the investments, debts, or other obligations from investors.
sentences.zh: 当循环被用来向投资者隐藏投资、债务或其他义务的影响时，它就变得尤其邪恶。

sentences.en: Figure 1: Google's backstopping of TeraWulf bonds, which are enabling the building of Fluidstack data centers leased by Anthropic. [original]
sentences.zh: 图 1：Google 对 TeraWulf 债券的支持，使 Anthropic 租赁的 Fluidstack 数据中心的建设成为可能。 [原来的]

blocks.html_en: Figure 1 shows the FT's[15] breakdown of a recent TeraWulf bond deal. In this case, TeraWulf can obtain financing given Google's backstop of any lease failures, should Fluidstack not be able to pay TeraWulf, or Anthropic unable to pay Fluidstack[16]. Google is skipping the entire reselling process and simply committing to cover any delinquencies. This gives TeraWulf the benefits of Google acting as a guarantor of the loan without the loan appearing on Google's balance sheet.

sentences.en: Figure 1 shows the FT's[15] breakdown of a recent TeraWulf bond deal.
sentences.zh: 图 1 显示了《金融时报》[15] 对最近 TeraWulf 债券交易的详细分析。

sentences.en: In this case, TeraWulf can obtain financing given Google's backstop of any lease failures, should Fluidstack not be able to pay TeraWulf, or Anthropic unable to pay Fluidstack[16].
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，如果 Fluidstack 无法支付 TeraWulf，或者 Anthropic 无法支付 Fluidstack[16]，TeraWulf 可以获得融资，因为 Google 有任何租赁失败的支持。

sentences.en: Google is skipping the entire reselling process and simply committing to cover any delinquencies.
sentences.zh: 谷歌跳过了整个转售过程，只是承诺弥补任何拖欠款项。

sentences.en: This gives TeraWulf the benefits of Google acting as a guarantor of the loan without the loan appearing on Google's balance sheet.
sentences.zh: 这使 TeraWulf 能够享受到 Google 作为贷款担保人的好处，而贷款不会出现在 Google 的资产负债表上。

blocks.html_en: Similarly, Meta's $27.3 billion Hyperion data center bond sale is an off-balance sheet one[17], as is its more recent $12.3 billion deal marketed by BlackRock[18].

sentences.en: Similarly, Meta's $27.3 billion Hyperion data center bond sale is an off-balance sheet one[17], as is its more recent $12.3 billion deal marketed by BlackRock[18].
sentences.zh: 同样，Meta 的 273 亿美元 Hyperion 数据中心债券销售也是资产负债表外债券[17]，贝莱德最近推出的 123 亿美元交易也是如此[18]。

blocks.html_en: Many finance professionals argue that these bonds are ultimately guaranteed by the impressive and continually growing revenues and profits from the hyperscalers, so there is nothing to worry about. The reason these bonds find so many customers, despite the circularity label, is that the final guarantors (i.e., the hyperscalers) generate billions of dollars of profit every year and can easily cover these costs, should it come down to that.

sentences.en: Many finance professionals argue that these bonds are ultimately guaranteed by the impressive and continually growing revenues and profits from the hyperscalers, so there is nothing to worry about.
sentences.zh: 许多金融专业人士认为，这些债券最终是由超大规模企业令人印象深刻且持续增长的收入和利润来保证的，因此没有什么可担心的。

sentences.en: The reason these bonds find so many customers, despite the circularity label, is that the final guarantors (i.e., the hyperscalers) generate billions of dollars of profit every year and can easily cover these costs, should it come down to that.
sentences.zh: 尽管带有循环性标签，这些债券仍能找到如此多客户的原因是，最终担保人（即超大规模企业）每年产生数十亿美元的利润，并且可以轻松支付这些成本（如果归根结底的话）。

blocks.html_en: … but this is today, and it's with the current bond deals. Will tomorrow's bond deals be supported by the hyperscalers in the same way? And what happens if hyperscaler revenue trends change? What if the banks begin expanding the backstop agreements from hyperscalers to “generally pretty decent” companies? What if the backstop fails to be enforced? Will we see hyperscaler-backstop-backed-bonds grouped together, collateralized, and resold the way Mortgage Backed Securities were in 2007?[19]

sentences.en: but this is today, and it's with the current bond deals.
sentences.zh: 但这就是今天，而且是当前的债券交易。

sentences.en: Will tomorrow's bond deals be supported by the hyperscalers in the same way?
sentences.zh: 明天的债券交易会以同样的方式得到超大规模交易者的支持吗？

sentences.en: And what happens if hyperscaler revenue trends change?
sentences.zh: 如果超大规模企业的收入趋势发生变化，会发生什么？

sentences.en: What if the banks begin expanding the backstop agreements from hyperscalers to “generally pretty decent” companies?
sentences.zh: 如果银行开始将支持协议从超大规模企业扩大到“总体相当不错”的公司怎么办？

sentences.en: What if the backstop fails to be enforced?
sentences.zh: 如果保障措施未能得到执行怎么办？

sentences.en: Will we see hyperscaler-backstop-backed-bonds grouped together, collateralized, and resold the way Mortgage Backed Securities were in 2007?[19]
sentences.zh: 我们会看到超大规模支持者支持的债券像 2007 年抵押贷款支持证券那样组合在一起、抵押并转售吗？[19]

blocks.html_en: Implications and Conclusion

sentences.en: Implications and Conclusion
sentences.zh: 影响和结论

blocks.html_en: Circular deals are not bad. In fact, they are critical in the development of the AI ecosystem much like such deals are used in critical minerals, oil, electric vehicles, and other capital intensive industries with incredibly high startup costs.

sentences.en: Circular deals are not bad.
sentences.zh: 循环交易也不错。

sentences.en: In fact, they are critical in the development of the AI ecosystem much like such deals are used in critical minerals, oil, electric vehicles, and other capital intensive industries with incredibly high startup costs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们对于人工智能生态系统的发展至关重要，就像此类交易用于关键矿产、石油、电动汽车和其他启动成本极高的资本密集型行业一样。

blocks.html_en: The circularity helps illustrate the commodification of AI today, and how the technology might one day be more like electricity or an internet connection, rather than a product one buys or subscribes to.

sentences.en: The circularity helps illustrate the commodification of AI today, and how the technology might one day be more like electricity or an internet connection, rather than a product one buys or subscribes to.
sentences.zh: 这种循环性有助于说明当今人工智能的商品化，以及这项技术有一天可能更像电力或互联网连接，而不是人们购买或订阅的产品。

blocks.html_en: When circular deals are supported by overextended lenders, or when overextended lenders try to move such deals off their balance sheets, they become ugly and bad—in other words, incredibly risky. This industry is likely to grow much more in the coming years, so it is important to watch for the lowering of standards or aggregation of risk. As SemiAnalysis writes[11]:

sentences.en: When circular deals are supported by overextended lenders, or when overextended lenders try to move such deals off their balance sheets, they become ugly and bad—in other words, incredibly risky.
sentences.zh: 当循环交易得到过度扩张的贷方支持时，或者当过度扩张的贷方试图将此类交易从其资产负债表中移出时，它们就会变得丑陋且糟糕——换句话说，风险极高。

sentences.en: This industry is likely to grow much more in the coming years, so it is important to watch for the lowering of standards or aggregation of risk.
sentences.zh: 该行业在未来几年可能会增长得更多，因此重要的是要注意标准的降低或风险的聚集。

sentences.en: As SemiAnalysis writes[11]:
sentences.zh: 正如 SemiAnalysis 所写[11]：

blocks.html_en: AI Debt Financing will become a multi-trillion-dollar credit market, with over $7T of debt outstanding by 2029 driven both by AI IT Capex and AI Datacenter Capex needs [...] This will make it the second largest asset backed debt market after the US mortgage-backed financing market at just over $13T.

sentences.en: AI Debt Financing will become a multi-trillion-dollar credit market, with over $7T of debt outstanding by 2029 driven both by AI IT Capex and AI Datacenter Capex needs [...]
sentences.zh: 人工智能债务融资将成为一个数万亿美元的信贷市场，到 2029 年，在人工智能 IT 资本支出和人工智能数据中心资本支出需求的推动下，未偿债务将超过 7T 美元 [...]

sentences.en: This will make it the second largest asset backed debt market after the US mortgage-backed financing market at just over $13T.
sentences.zh: 这将使其成为仅次于美国抵押贷款支持融资市场的第二大资产支持债务市场，其规模略高于 13T。

blocks.html_en: In this evolution, there might be a few bad deals along the way. It's important to keep your eyes open.

sentences.en: In this evolution, there might be a few bad deals along the way.
sentences.zh: 在这一演变过程中，可能会出现一些糟糕的交易。

sentences.en: It's important to keep your eyes open.

content_html_zh:
每隔几个月，尤其是本周，人工智能领域就会因循环融资和客户关系而受到批评。 OpenAI 从微软筹集资金，用于购买微软服务器； Nvidia 支持 CoreWeave 债务，CoreWeave 购买 Nvidia GPU。 “泡沫即将破灭！” 分析师尖叫。

分析师指出 1999 年的网络交易涉及循环投资，认为这一切肯定会再次发生[1][2]。 他们错了。

循环交易比“好”或“坏”更有趣。 它们表明人工智能行业不仅正在成熟，而且正在将“人工智能”的概念修改为不再是技术产品，而是更多的商品。 想象一下——像电力一样可用的智能，以及相应构建的底层金融系统。

循环交易的演变指向人工智能的商品化，其中计算能力正在从购买产品（例如硬件或数据中心空间）的商业模式转变为可替代的东西，以至于您可以像购买电力、铜、天然气或其他商品一​​样购买它。

我们将探讨为什么循环交易在大宗商品行业中特别重要，以及这对于理解人工智能的发展轨迹意味着什么。 首先，我们将介绍传统大宗商品市场的主要投资如何发挥作用，以便更清楚地为我们的类比奠定基础。 接下来，我们将介绍在人工智能领域模仿这一过程的投资，展示此类投资如何保持健康。 最后，我们将探讨一些循环交易不遵守这一类比的例子，以及这些交易如何引入风险，这些风险有一天可能会给公司本身、投资者或整个行业带来可怕的意外。

买卖商品：循环入门

矿山、炼油厂和港口等复杂的商品基础设施伴随着巨大的开发成本，以至于银行向开发公司贷款可能会冒着自身偿付能力的风险。 与多个客户或受益人甚至可能是政府的循环交易往往是唯一导致铲子陷入泥土或船只陷入水中的解决方案。

让我们看一下此类交易的一个简化示例。 想象一下，您想通过几口井和一条管道来发展您所在地区的经济，但您负担不起。 您与一家商品贸易公司合作，该公司同意通过保证银行或债券买家将以一定价格购买您的所有石油，从而使您的公司对银行或债券买家有吸引力。 这意味着您在可预见的未来可以获得收入保证，并且银行知道他们可以相信您会偿还贷款。 出于良好的考虑，贸易公司甚至可能会持有您公司的股权——这可能是为了鼓励更好的治理或监督。

通过你和石油贸易商之间的这种关系，你可以获得石油、一大笔银行贷款和一个有保障的客户…… 您已经获得了循环商品交易！

这不是一个人为的例子；这是自 20 世纪 60 年代以来制定和发展的共同战略。 日本大宗商品贸易商和开发银行为基础设施提供资金以支持大宗商品开发，并承诺未来的购买和股权交易[3]。 牙买加在 20 世纪 80 年代就这样做了[4]。

最近，美国政府开始促进循环交易，以刺激关键矿产行业，以增强供应链的弹性。 去年，磁铁制造和关键矿物领域相对较新的 MP Materials 宣布与美国陆军部建立为期 10 年的合作关系，后者承诺以至少 110 美元/公斤的价格从该公司购买所有钕镨（即磁铁）[5]。 此后，MP Materials 和通用汽车之间宣布了此类承购协议[6]，并且实际上在电动汽车领域非常常见[7]。 这些直接关系还激励了大宗商品生产商甚至底层矿山的股权，因为很明显这些生产商和矿山将在未来几年获得收入。

具有大型全球市场的可替代商品特别适合此类交易，因为保证成为客户的交易对手（即上面示例中的石油贸易公司）知道他们可以进入一个巨大的市场。 他们可能有成功进行此类销售的历史，否则他们就不会拥有数十亿美元和可以利用的原始声誉。

人工智能是可替代的且开发成本昂贵

前沿的生成式 AI 行业——无论是模型开发还是推理——都非常依赖 Nvidia。 由于 Nvidia 开发了底层基础设施以及该领域所有公司的标准化，GPU 实际上是一种可替代的商品。 三种力量使人工智能芯片和相关数据中心能够像可替代商品一样发挥作用：

  1. 如今，大部分计算都来自 Nvidia GPU，因此对于超大规模用户、模型构建者和需要推理的用户来说，使用相似芯片的两个数据中心几乎是相同的。
  2. 大规模模型开发和推理需要大型数据中心，有时成本远超 100 亿美元。 除非通过创造性的融资交易或通过拥有巨额财富的公司（即超大规模企业），否则无法开发这些数据中心。
  3. 除了GPU、内存和其他硬件之外，电力是另一个瓶颈。 如果没有大量可靠的电力，就无法建造 11 位数的数据中心。

因此，GPU、电力和数据中心都可以有效地替代，并且存在大量订单积压和被压抑的需求。 如果您构建了一个数据中心，但无法将其用于自己的业务，那么您很有可能将其出售给有能力的人，他们甚至可能会在短期内为可用性支付溢价。

SpaceX 和 Meta 尽管试图构建顶级基础模型，但仍将自己的数据中心出租给其他公司以盈利——这些数据中心目前正在运行，并为前沿实验室工作负载做好了准备。 资本充足的实验室愿意为这一特权支付巨额溢价。 SpaceX 以每月超过 20 亿美元的价格租赁其 Colossus 1 和 2 数据中心[8]，其价格远高于其他小型云和数据中心[9]。

现在让我们回到有抱负的初创公司 Neocloud。 您正在起步，就像我们之前的石油示例一样，已经在小规模上证明了自己，但现在需要自己的数据中心或访问数千个 GPU。 你能做什么？

英伟达和循环交易很像石油交易。

Nvidia 为您的初创公司提供资金和产品访问权限，优先让您访问其 GPU，以便您可以获得所需的硬件。 Nvidia 拥有 1 万亿美元的积压订单[10]，并且知道如果您失败了，它可以转售您的硬件或更好地利用它，因此它更进一步：如果您无法利用它，它就会成为您的计算的保证买家...... 就像上面的 SpaceX 和 Meta 一样。 这不是理论上的——SemiAnalysis 提供了 Nvidia 计算承购协议和定价的估算[11]。 与我们的石油例子一样，英伟达可能也想要一些股权——如果你以后需要寻求任何帮助，你会希望他们拥有这些股权。

当然，这是一种循环交易，而且是一种相对简单的交易。 它已被用于 CoreWeave 与 Nvidia 的 63 亿美元交易[12]，以及 Firmus 等小型数据中心运营商（5.05 亿美元[13]）。

这有助于解释为什么我们看到如此多的互连和循环关系——OpenAI 取消了与 Oracle 的交易，因此 Meta 突然介入[14]； SpaceX向谷歌租赁服务器，谷歌投资Anthropic；等等。

华尔街获得循环交易，人类获得通用人工智能…… 据称。

当循环交易变得丑陋时

英伟达声称它正在支持全球人工智能生态系统。 不幸的是，这并不妨碍它过度扩张。 与 CoreWeave 达成 63 亿美元的交易是一回事，但承诺高达 7500 亿美元[2] 则是另一回事。

这种方法对于初创公司和新云的成功还假设人工智能和数据中心继续可替代和“可转售”。 如果标准或芯片组发生变化，或者技术应该使本地模型或小型集群上的模型更容易运行，那么商业模式可能会失败，而英伟达的承购协议可能不会对生态系统有太大帮助。

… 当他们变坏时

当循环被用来向投资者隐藏投资、债务或其他义务的影响时，它就变得尤其邪恶。

图 1 显示了《金融时报》[15] 对最近 TeraWulf 债券交易的详细分析。 在这种情况下，如果 Fluidstack 无法支付 TeraWulf，或者 Anthropic 无法支付 Fluidstack[16]，TeraWulf 可以获得融资，因为 Google 有任何租赁失败的支持。 谷歌跳过了整个转售过程，只是承诺弥补任何拖欠款项。 这使 TeraWulf 能够享受到 Google 作为贷款担保人的好处，而贷款不会出现在 Google 的资产负债表上。

同样，Meta 的 273 亿美元 Hyperion 数据中心债券销售也是资产负债表外债券[17]，贝莱德最近推出的 123 亿美元交易也是如此[18]。

许多金融专业人士认为，这些债券最终是由超大规模企业令人印象深刻且持续增长的收入和利润来保证的，因此没有什么可担心的。 尽管带有循环性标签，这些债券仍能找到如此多客户的原因是，最终担保人（即超大规模企业）每年产生数十亿美元的利润，并且可以轻松支付这些成本（如果归根结底的话）。

… 但这就是今天，而且是当前的债券交易。 明天的债券交易会以同样的方式得到超大规模交易者的支持吗？ 如果超大规模企业的收入趋势发生变化，会发生什么？ 如果银行开始将支持协议从超大规模企业扩大到“总体相当不错”的公司怎么办？ 如果保障措施未能得到执行怎么办？ 我们会看到超大规模支持者支持的债券像 2007 年抵押贷款支持证券那样组合在一起、抵押并转售吗？[19]

影响和结论

循环交易也不错。 事实上，它们对于人工智能生态系统的发展至关重要，就像此类交易用于关键矿产、石油、电动汽车和其他启动成本极高的资本密集型行业一样。

这种循环性有助于说明当今人工智能的商品化，以及这项技术有一天可能更像电力或互联网连接，而不是人们购买或订阅的产品。

当循环交易得到过度扩张的贷方支持时，或者当过度扩张的贷方试图将此类交易从其资产负债表中移出时，它们就会变得丑陋且糟糕——换句话说，风险极高。 该行业在未来几年可能会增长得更多，因此重要的是要注意标准的降低或风险的聚集。 正如 SemiAnalysis 所写[11]：

人工智能债务融资将成为一个数万亿美元的信贷市场，到 2029 年，在人工智能 IT 资本支出和人工智能数据中心资本支出需求的推动下，未偿债务将超过 7T 美元 [...] 这将使其成为仅次于美国抵押贷款支持融资市场的第二大资产支持债务市场，其规模略高于 13T。

在这一演变过程中，可能会出现一些糟糕的交易。 睁大眼睛很重要。
